samples.summary: The canonical REST-API design doc now contradicts the code this delta adds. `rest-api.md` §"PUT validation contract" states that on the slides walk "the structural block checks (`id`, `inlines`, a present `style`) are not applied" — deliberately relaxed so a GET→edit→PUT round-trip of an older deck cannot 400. This delta adds `assertValidSlideInlines` (docs-content.controller.ts:704/741), which does hold a *present* `inlines` on a slide block to a contract (array of objects, string `text`, object `style`), i.e. a structural check on `inlines` in the slides arm. The doc was not updated in the same change (the sibling DOCX doc *was* updated for `toHeadingStyleId`), leaving the documented contract wrong and the new relaxation boundary (present-only vs required) unrecorded. It also silently narrows the stated round-trip guarantee: a legacy deck whose stored inline lacks `text` now 400s on re-PUT, which the doc explicitly says must not happen.

samples.summary: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts` now routes every `<a:clrScheme>` slot value through `toRgbHexColor` with a `000000` fallback (a behavior change: a stored theme color the normalizer cannot express now exports as black instead of being passed through). `slides-pptx-export.md` §3 maintains an explicit taxonomy of color sinks — "omittable sinks drop the color" vs "mandatory sinks fall back to 000000" — and §5 still describes the theme as a plain `ColorScheme → <a:clrScheme>` mapping. The new mandatory sink and its fallback are not recorded there, even though the parallel DOCX change in this same delta did add a converter/failure-behavior row to `docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md`. The closed-`Map` attribute lookups added here (routing `prst`, arrowhead kind/size, `prstDash`, layout `type`) are likewise undocumented in that doc's round-trip tables.

The delta's stated design principle — "attribute lookups over persisted JSON must be closed `Map`s with an explicit fallback, because an object literal consults the prototype chain and an unknown key emits `undefined`" — is applied to connector routing/arrowheads, shape dash and layout type, but sibling sinks in the same exporter are left as bare object literals with no fallback at all: `animation.ts` `TYPE_TO_TAG[t.type]` (line 90), `DIR_TO_ATTR[t.direction]` (line 95), `CATEGORY_TO_CLASS`/`START_TO_NODE_TYPE`/`EFFECT_TO_PRESET`, and `color.ts` `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` (color.ts:49) — whose own comment at color.ts:31 already asserts it is "a closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value" and whose doc comment claims an "unknown-`role` arm" fallback that does not exist in code. Applying the hardening pattern to a subset leaves the exporter inconsistent and the invariant the comments claim untrue.

`assertValidSlideInlines` re-implements, near-verbatim, the inline loop already inside `assertValidBlock` (same file, lines 419–442) — same three checks, same message strings, differing only in that `inlines` and `style` may be absent. A single shared helper parameterized by strictness (the file already does this for `assertValidBlockStyle`, which takes an alignment-strictness argument) would keep the two arms' error messages and tolerances from drifting.

`toHeadingStyleId` is the third heading-level normalizer in `packages/docs` with a third behavior: `serialize/markdown.ts:128` `clampHeadingLevel` clamps out-of-range to 1/6, `model/named-styles.ts:108` clamps with `Math.min(6, Math.max(1, …))`, and the new one drops the style entirely. None is shared. If `HeadingLevel` needs runtime narrowing (the premise of this change), it belongs once in `model/` next to `toRgbHexColor` — which is exactly the reuse pattern the sibling color fix in this same delta follows.

The same untrusted `block.headingLevel` reaches the PDF outline builder as `level: b.headingLevel ?? 1` with no range check, while this delta hardens only the DOCX `<w:pStyle>` sink. If the premise is that persisted `headingLevel` may be `NaN` or out of range (the doc comment cites the CRDT `Number(...)` coercion), the PDF outline sink has the same exposure and is left uncovered, so the hardening is partial rather than a property of the model.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree: `assertValidSlideInlines` (docs-content.controller.ts:741-770, called at :704) applies a structural contract to a *present* `inlines` on a slide block — array (:743), entries objects (:750), `text` must be a string (:755), present `style` must be an object (:760). The canonical doc `docs/design/rest-api.md:253-259` still says that on the slides walk "the structural block checks (`id`, `inlines`, a present `style`) are not applied", justified by the requirement that a GET→edit→PUT round-trip of an older deck must not 400. A legacy deck whose stored inline lacks `text` now 400s at :755, and no doc anywhere records the new present-only relaxation boundary. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: `grep inlines docs/` returns only Block-model prose in docs/slides/pagination/IME docs; `grep 'validation contract|assertValid|structural block checks'` repo-wide hits only rest-api.md:227 and the controller; docs/design/backend.md and docs/design/slides/*.md contain no PUT-validation text; no docs/tasks/active file covers this delta. Confidence is low, not high, because rest-api.md:232-235 does already state the general "an inline needs a string `text`" contract, and the relaxation sentence can be read as relaxing only presence requirements — under that reading the new check is partly pre-described. Even so the doc remains inaccurate in the other direction (it says a slide inline needs a `style` object, whereas the code checks it only when present) and its stated no-400 round-trip rationale is silently narrowed, so I cannot produce a refuting counterexample.

verdict.reason: The code change is real: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:76-78 routes every clrScheme slot through toRgbHexColor with a '000000' fallback (applied at :94-99), creating a new mandatory color sink with fail-to-black behavior. The design doc that owns this subsystem keeps an explicit sink taxonomy at docs/design/slides/slides-pptx-export.md:158-169 (omittable sinks drop the color; mandatory sinks = 'shape / gradient-stop / background fills' fall back to 000000) and §5 at :196-198 still describes the theme as a plain ColorScheme -> <a:clrScheme> mapping; neither mentions the theme slots or the new fallback. Repo-wide greps of docs/ for clrScheme|toRgbHexColor|srgbClr and of docs/design/ for toSrgbHex|mandatory sink|000000|injection|normaliz turned up no other doc recording it — docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md:436-454 documents only the DOCX sinks and cross-references the PPTX doc generically at :453, and slides-themes-layouts-import.md covers the import direction. So no counterexample exists for the core claim, and the parallel DOCX row in the same delta shows the repo's own convention here. Note the secondary sub-claim is partly inaccurate: the prst map (:184), connector routing prstGeom (:188) and layout type/matchingName (:200-202, :277) ARE documented; only the arrowhead maps (connector.ts:45,64) and prstDash (shape.ts:132) are not — that weakens but does not refute the finding.

verdict.reason: Every checkable claim holds. animation.ts declares TYPE_TO_TAG (53), DIR_TO_ATTR (72), CATEGORY_TO_CLASS (111), EFFECT_TO_PRESET (121), START_TO_NODE_TYPE (149) as bare object literals and reads them without fallback at lines 90, 95, 177, 191, interpolating the result directly into OOXML tag/attribute positions. color.ts:4 declares ROLE_TO_SCHEME as a Record and reads it unguarded at :49. The contrasted siblings genuinely use the hardened form with explicit fallbacks: connector.ts:15/45/64 read at :72/:73/:93, shape.ts:24 read at :97, shape.ts:132 read at :153 — and their comments (connector.ts:10-13, shape.ts:20-22, shape.ts:125-130) state the principle. The comment claims are also accurate: color.ts:31 asserts a "closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value" and color.ts:58 plus docs/design/slides/slides-pptx-export.md:165-167 both assert an unknown-role fallback that does not exist in colorChildXml. The only role validation is text.ts:200-219, which sits on the omittable text path; the mandatory sinks (fillXml/solidFillXml at color.ts:63,91, used by shape/background/gradient) receive model ThemeColor from persisted JSON unvalidated, so already-guarded does not apply. I weighed out-of-scope (security-lens overlap) but the finding is also a documented-invariant-vs-code conformance gap, which is in this lens's lane, and the originating issue's acceptance criteria were not supplied, so I cannot exclude that the hardening principle is itself the criterion.
